subject.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers

question: Should same-label system LaunchDaemon presence—or an unverifiable system-domain state—unconditionally block user LaunchAgent install, stage, bootstrap repair, and activation even when `--force` is supplied?
rationale: The guard fixes a deterministic restart-loop bug, but it deliberately converts previously permissive operator workflows into fail-closed errors that can require privileged cleanup; repository policy treats that fallback and compatibility choice as maintainer-owned.

options.title: Accept the narrow guard
options.body: Merge the fail-closed duplicate-manager prevention after rebase and exact-head checks, while leaving full system LaunchDaemon lifecycle support to the existing broader issues.

options.title: Add an explicit override policy
options.body: Require a separately named advanced escape hatch with clear warnings and focused tests instead of allowing ordinary `--force` to bypass ownership checks.

options.title: Wait for unified lifecycle design
options.body: Pause this PR until system and user launchd install, status, stop, restart, and uninstall semantics are designed together.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow guard
recommendation.body: Merge the fail-closed duplicate-manager prevention after rebase and exact-head checks, while leaving full system LaunchDaemon lifecycle support to the existing broader issues.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned, requested re-review, contributed the activation-conflict implementation, and have recent history in the affected launchd surface.
